items.title: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026: Audible Wants to Turn Every Book into an Audiobook
items.excerpt: Audible CCO Rachel Ghiazza says the company expects to use AI tools across the entire audiobook production process to reach 'every book in every language', and will launch in Indonesia, South Korea, Denmark, Norway and Finland in 2027.
items.rationale: Audible, the largest audiobook platform, says it will put AI across the whole production pipeline to reach every book in every language. It is also launching in South Korea. This is the strongest article in the Audible Frankfurt cluster.

items.title: Book Publishers Are Quietly Using More AI. Staff Are Revolting
items.excerpt: Workers at three major publishing houses tell WIRED that LLMs are being used for publicity, cover art, back cover copy and emails, as some execs push junior staff to champion the tech.
items.rationale: New reporting from inside three major publishing houses: LLMs are already writing publicity copy, cover art and back-cover copy, and staff are pushing back. It covers more than the single S&S performance-tracking story.

items.title: Neues Label: "Von Menschen gemacht"
items.excerpt: 18 German-language children's and YA publishers launch a 'Von Menschen - geschrieben - gestaltet - geprüft' label certifying that text, illustration and design are human-made and editorially checked.
items.rationale: 18 German children's and YA publishers have launched a joint label certifying that text, illustration and design are human-made. It is a separate launch from the UK IPO human-authored mark, by different publishers in a different market.

items.title: Ghostwriters haunted by AI as commissions fall and machine-written manuscripts rise
items.excerpt: Ghostwriters tell The Bookseller that commissions are falling as prospective authors experiment with generative AI, while others are increasingly asked to rework AI-generated manuscripts.
items.rationale: Reporting on a profession being reshaped right now: ghostwriting commissions are falling, and the work is moving to fixing AI-generated manuscripts. The brief has not covered ghostwriting before.

items.title: Frankfurter Buchmesse 2026: Tonies Bets On a Kids' Audio Future that Is Screenless, Serialized, with Content (Often) Made In-house
items.excerpt: Tonies trialed an AI 'storyteller' with 3,000 households generating personalized children's stories, and 85% of staff use AI daily, but CEO Tobias Wann insists the Toniebox 'will never become an AI toy'.
items.rationale: Hard numbers from a kids' audio leader: an AI storyteller trial generating personalized stories for 3,000 households, and 85% of staff using AI daily. The CEO still draws a line at making the Toniebox an AI toy.
